title: Determine Whether Matrix Can Be Obtained By Rotation
summary: Evaluate if matrix mat can be transformed into matrix target through sequential 90-degree rotations, returning true if possible, otherwise false.
statement: Evaluate if matrix mat can be transformed into matrix target through sequential 90-degree rotations, returning true if possible, otherwise false.
constraints: Both inputs are square matrices of equal size from 1 through 10.
Cells contain only zero or one.
Allowed transformations are zero, one, two, or three clockwise 90-degree rotations.
reference_solution:
def can_obtain_matrix_by_rotation(mat, target):
    size = len(mat)
    matches_zero = matches_one = matches_two = matches_three = True
    for row in range(size):
        for column in range(size):
            value = target[row][column]
            matches_zero &= mat[row][column] == value
            matches_one &= mat[size - 1 - column][row] == value
            matches_two &= mat[size - 1 - row][size - 1 - column] == value
            matches_three &= mat[column][size - 1 - row] == value
    return matches_zero or matches_one or matches_two or matches_three
hints: There are only four distinct orientations of a square under repeated quarter turns.
For each target cell, compare the corresponding source coordinate in all four rotations.
Keep a flag for each orientation and return true if any flag survives every cell.
The coordinate mappings cover exactly 0, 90, 180, and 270 degrees; a surviving flag is therefore necessary and sufficient.
editorial: The coordinate mappings cover exactly 0, 90, 180, and 270 degrees; a surviving flag is therefore necessary and sufficient.

tests.explanation: One clockwise rotation transforms mat into target.
None of the four orientations matches every target cell.
